chapter: Army band, Lena Horne, Billie Holiday and the 1950s
title: Arranging for Barnet again; Ford Leary's laryngitis before the Paramount
summary: In 1943-44 Horace wrote for Charlie Barnet, whose band had Billy May and Cliff Leeman. When trombonist-singer Ford Leary lost his voice before a Paramount booking, Barnet sent Horace to Harlem to find a singer.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: Following that time then, you played again off and on for a couple of years -- '43 and '44 -- in Fletcher's band, and then I note here that you reformed your group -- smaller group, and from time to time you were

Yes. Along that era, I believe I was doing quite a bit of arranging for Charley Barnet and his great band, you know, and Billy May was in that band, the great arranger and trumpet player. Course Charley had some great guys that could play, and of course, I think that Cliff Leeman, drum --

He was in that band when I was connected with it, and of course, that is where I ran into Lena Horne. Charley Barnet was in New York City, and he had a trombone player with him at that time that played trombone with a valve -- a bass trombone where you could hit that low note with that key, you know, and his name was Ford Leary. A big guy. He had four trombone players, and Ford Leary was the guy that Barnet featured singing Shadrack.

So I never will forget this. Charley was booked to go in the Paramount Theatre, and Dinah Shore was on the bill as extra added attraction. Well, I'm a little ahead of myself, but to get the band set for this particular engagement at the Paramount in New York City, he took a job in a theatre uptown in the Bronx called the Valencia Theatre. So

Charlie called me, and he says, "Horace, I don't know what we're gonna do. Ford Leary, my trombonist and vocalist, has suffered a severe case of laryngitis." He says, "You think you could find me a singer? Go down to Harlem somewhere, down to the Apollo Theatre, and find me a singer." I said, "Well, I'll try." So I got in my car and I drove down, and to make a long story short, after enquiring around, guess who I came back with?
